result.instructions: This server edits a program of an AKAI S5000/S6000 sampler. Call get_status to see which program is current, list_programs and select_program to change it, and list_parameters to learn the parameter names and what each accepts: the filter, the amplitude envelope, the filter envelope and the two LFOs. Use get_parameters to read values and set_parameter to change one. Values are in the sampler's own units (0 to 100 for most), signed values are plain signed numbers, and choices are named as the sampler's screen names them (for example "2-POLE LP+"). create_program, rename_program and delete_program change the list of programs: delete_program deletes only the current program and only when its name is given as 'confirm'. list_samples, select_sample, get_sample_parameters and set_sample_parameter edit the samples in the same way (list_parameters with the domain "sample" names their parameters); no tool creates, deletes or loads a sample. list_multis, select_multi, get_multi_parameters and set_multi_parameter edit the parts of a multi (parts are numbered from 1; no tool creates, deletes or renames a multi). Changes act on the sampler's memory, not on disk; nothing is saved by this server.

tools.description: Says whether the sampler answers, how many programs are in its memory and which one is current (with its number of keygroups). Call it first.
tools.name: get_status
tools.title: Sampler status

tools.description: Lists the programs in the sampler's memory with their positions (from 0).
tools.name: list_programs
tools.title: List programs

tools.description: Makes a program of the sampler's memory the current one, by its name or its position (from 0, see list_programs). Every later edit acts on it. Give exactly one of name and index. It acts on the sampler's memory, not on disk: nothing is saved, and the change is lost if the sampler is switched off without saving the program from its front panel.
tools.name: select_program
tools.title: Select a program

tools.description: Lists the parameters that can be read and set: their names, what they accept and what they do. Call it before get_parameters or set_parameter to learn the names, and optionally give a group to list only that group. The parameters are those of a program (the default) unless a domain is given.

domain.description: What the parameters belong to: "program" (the default), "sample" (the current sample's), "multi" (a part of the current multi).

group.description: One group of the domain: for a program filter, amplitude envelope, filter envelope, lfo 1, lfo 2, keygroup, pitch and amplitude, aux envelope, output, tuning, pitch bend, zone ("lfo" is both LFOs).

tools.name: list_parameters
tools.title: List parameters

tools.description: Reads the current values of parameters of the current program: a whole group, or a list of parameter names (see list_parameters). Give exactly one of group and parameters. Reading a keygroup parameter moves the sampler's current keygroup selection.

keygroup.description: Which keygroup of the current program: a number from 1, or "all" (the default). It applies to the keygroup and zone parameters (filter, envelopes, zones); the LFO parameters belong to the program.

parameters.description: Parameter names, for example ["filter cutoff", "filter resonance"].

zone.description: Which zone of the keygroup(s), 1 to 4, or "all" (the default). Only for the zone parameters (group "zone").

tools.name: get_parameters
tools.title: Read parameters

tools.description: Sets one parameter of the current program (see list_parameters for the names and what each accepts), then reads it back from the sampler and reports what it holds. The value is a number in the sampler's own units, or the name of a choice such as "2-POLE LP+", or on/off. Nothing is sent when the name or the value is not valid. It acts on the sampler's memory, not on disk: nothing is saved, and the change is lost if the sampler is switched off without saving the program from its front panel.

keygroup.description: Which keygroup of the current program: a number from 1, or "all" (the default). It applies to the keygroup and zone parameters (filter, envelopes, zones); the LFO parameters belong to the program.

parameter.description: The parameter's name, for example "filter cutoff".

value.description: A number, a choice label, or on/off (true/false).

zone.description: Which zone of the keygroup(s), 1 to 4, or "all" (the default). Only for the zone parameters (group "zone").

tools.name: set_parameter
tools.title: Set a parameter

tools.description: Creates a new program with the given name and number of keygroups (1 to 99) and makes it the current program, so the next edits act on it. It acts on the sampler's memory, not on disk: nothing is saved, and the change is lost if the sampler is switched off without saving the program from its front panel.

keygroups.description: How many keygroups the program has, 1 to 99.

name.description: The new program's name, 1 to 12 characters.

tools.name: create_program
tools.title: Create a program

tools.description: Renames the current program (see get_status) and reads the new name back. It acts on the sampler's memory, not on disk: nothing is saved, and the change is lost if the sampler is switched off without saving the program from its front panel.
tools.name: rename_program
tools.title: Rename the current program

tools.description: Deletes the CURRENT program (see get_status), and only if 'confirm' is exactly its name: otherwise nothing is deleted and the answer says which program is current. It cannot be undone from here. It acts on the sampler's memory, not on disk: nothing is saved, and the change is lost if the sampler is switched off without saving the program from its front panel.

confirm.description: The exact name of the current program, to confirm the deletion.

tools.name: delete_program
tools.title: Delete the current program

tools.description: Lists the samples in the sampler's memory with their positions (from 0) and says which one is current.
tools.name: list_samples
tools.title: List samples

tools.description: Makes a sample of the sampler's memory the current one, by its name or its position (from 0, see list_samples). get_sample_parameters and set_sample_parameter act on it. Give exactly one of name and index. It acts on the sampler's memory, not on disk: nothing is saved, and the change is lost if the sampler is switched off without saving the program from its front panel.
tools.name: select_sample
tools.title: Select a sample

tools.description: Reads the current sample's parameters (see list_parameters with the domain "sample"): a whole group, or a list of parameter names. Give exactly one of group and parameters. Select a sample first.

parameters.description: Parameter names, for example ["sample loop start", "sample loop end"].

tools.name: get_sample_parameters
tools.title: Read sample parameters

tools.description: Sets one parameter of the current sample (see list_parameters with the domain "sample"), then reads it back from the sampler and reports what it holds. Positions are in sample points. Parameters of the group "info" are read-only. Select a sample first. It acts on the sampler's memory, not on disk: nothing is saved, and the change is lost if the sampler is switched off without saving the program from its front panel.

parameter.description: The parameter's name, for example "sample loop end".

value.description: A number, or a choice label such as "loop in rel".

tools.name: set_sample_parameter
tools.title: Set a sample parameter

tools.description: Lists the multis in the sampler's memory with their positions (from 0), says which one is current and how many parts it has.
tools.name: list_multis
tools.title: List multis

tools.description: Makes a multi of the sampler's memory the current one, by its name or its position (from 0, see list_multis). get_multi_parameters and set_multi_parameter act on it. Give exactly one of name and index. It acts on the sampler's memory, not on disk: nothing is saved, and the change is lost if the sampler is switched off without saving the program from its front panel.
tools.name: select_multi
tools.title: Select a multi

tools.description: Reads the parameters of the parts of the current multi (see list_parameters with the domain "multi"): a whole group, or a list of parameter names, for one part or for every part (the default). Give exactly one of group and parameters. Select a multi first.

parameters.description: Parameter names, for example ["part level", "part pan"].

part.description: Which part of the current multi: a number from 1, or "all".

tools.name: get_multi_parameters
tools.title: Read multi part parameters

tools.description: Sets one parameter of one part of the current multi (see list_parameters with the domain "multi"), or of every part with part "all", then reads it back from the sampler and reports what it holds. The part is required. Select a multi first. It acts on the sampler's memory, not on disk: nothing is saved, and the change is lost if the sampler is switched off without saving the program from its front panel.

parameter.description: The parameter's name, for example "part level".

part.description: Which part of the current multi: a number from 1, or "all".

value.description: A number, a choice label such as "10B" or "RV3", or on/off (true/false).

tools.name: set_multi_parameter
tools.title: Set a multi part parameter

tools.description: Assigns a sample of the sampler's memory to one of the four zones of a keygroup of the current program, so the keygroup plays it, and reads the assignment back. Load the sample first (load_file) and see list_samples for the names. It acts on the sampler's memory, not on disk: nothing is saved, and the change is lost if the sampler is switched off without saving the program from its front panel.

keygroup.description: The keygroup of the current program, from 1 (see get_status for how many).

tools.name: set_zone_sample
tools.title: Assign a sample to a zone

tools.description: Says which sample each of the four zones plays, for one keygroup of the current program or for all of them. It acts on the sampler's memory, not on disk: nothing is saved, and the change is lost if the sampler is switched off without saving the program from its front panel.

keygroup.description: One keygroup, from 1. Leave it out for every keygroup.

tools.name: get_zone_samples
tools.title: Read the samples of the zones

tools.description: Adds keygroups (empty, with the default settings) to the CURRENT program, up to the 99 a program can have, and says how many it has then. See get_status for the current program and its keygroups. It acts on the sampler's memory, not on disk: nothing is saved, and the change is lost if the sampler is switched off without saving the program from its front panel.
tools.name: add_keygroups
tools.title: Add keygroups to the current program

tools.description: Deletes one keygroup (with its settings and zones) of the CURRENT program, and only if 'confirm' is exactly the program's name: otherwise nothing is deleted and the answer says which program is current. The last keygroup of a program is never deleted. It cannot be undone from here. It acts on the sampler's memory, not on disk: nothing is saved, and the change is lost if the sampler is switched off without saving the program from its front panel.

confirm.description: The exact name of the current program, to confirm the deletion.

tools.name: delete_keygroup
tools.title: Delete a keygroup of the current program

tools.description: Starts or stops the audition of the CURRENT sample (see select_sample): the sampler plays it through its outputs. A started audition plays until it is stopped with action "stop". It acts on the sampler's memory, not on disk: nothing is saved, and the change is lost if the sampler is switched off without saving the program from its front panel.
tools.name: audition_sample
tools.title: Play or stop the current sample

tools.description: Says which sampler this is (S5000 or S6000), its operating system version and how much of its memory is free: the wave memory (percent and bytes: check it before loading a large sample) and the memory for programs, keygroups, samples and multis (percent). It changes nothing.
tools.name: get_system_info
tools.title: Read the sampler's model and memory

tools.description: Renames the CURRENT sample (see list_samples and select_sample) and reads the new name back. A name another sample already bears is refused. It acts on the sampler's memory, not on disk: nothing is saved, and the change is lost if the sampler is switched off without saving the program from its front panel.
tools.name: rename_sample
tools.title: Rename the current sample

tools.description: Deletes the CURRENT sample from the sampler's memory (see list_samples and select_sample), and only if 'confirm' is exactly its name: otherwise nothing is deleted and the answer says which sample is current. A sample that is not on a disk is lost; it cannot be undone from here. It acts on the sampler's memory, not on disk: nothing is saved, and the change is lost if the sampler is switched off without saving the program from its front panel.

confirm.description: The exact name of the current sample, to confirm the deletion.

tools.name: delete_sample
tools.title: Delete the current sample

tools.description: Creates an empty multi with the given name and makes it the current multi, so the next edits act on it (see set_part_program and set_multi_parameter). A name another multi bears is refused. It acts on the sampler's memory, not on disk: nothing is saved, and the change is lost if the sampler is switched off without saving the program from its front panel.

name.description: The new multi's name, 1 to 20 characters.

tools.name: create_multi
tools.title: Create a multi

tools.description: Renames the CURRENT multi (see list_multis and select_multi) and reads the new name back. A name another multi bears is refused. It acts on the sampler's memory, not on disk: nothing is saved, and the change is lost if the sampler is switched off without saving the program from its front panel.
tools.name: rename_multi
tools.title: Rename the current multi

tools.description: Deletes the CURRENT multi from the sampler's memory (see list_multis and select_multi), and only if 'confirm' is exactly its name: otherwise nothing is deleted and the answer says which multi is current. A multi that is not on a disk is lost; it cannot be undone from here. It acts on the sampler's memory, not on disk: nothing is saved, and the change is lost if the sampler is switched off without saving the program from its front panel.

confirm.description: The exact name of the current multi, to confirm the deletion.

tools.name: delete_multi
tools.title: Delete the current multi

tools.description: Makes one part of the CURRENT multi (see select_multi) play a program of the sampler's memory, and reads it back. Parts are numbered from 1. Give the program by 'program' (its name) or by 'position' (its place in list_programs, from 0), not both. It acts on the sampler's memory, not on disk: nothing is saved, and the change is lost if the sampler is switched off without saving the program from its front panel.

part.description: The part, from 1 (see list_multis for how many).

position.description: The program's position in list_programs, from 0.

tools.name: set_part_program
tools.title: Make a part of the current multi play a program

tools.description: Removes the program a part of the CURRENT multi plays (the multi stays), and only if 'confirm' is exactly the multi's name: otherwise nothing is removed and the answer says which multi is current. Parts are numbered from 1. It acts on the sampler's memory, not on disk: nothing is saved, and the change is lost if the sampler is switched off without saving the program from its front panel.

confirm.description: The exact name of the current multi, to confirm the removal.

tools.name: clear_part
tools.title: Remove the program of a part of the current multi

tools.description: Sets the CURRENT multi's program number (1 to 128, as on the front panel: the number a MIDI program change selects it by) or switches it off with null, and reads it back. It acts on the sampler's memory, not on disk: nothing is saved, and the change is lost if the sampler is switched off without saving the program from its front panel.

number.description: The number, 1 to 128, or null to switch it off.

tools.name: set_multi_program_number
tools.title: Set the program number of the current multi

tools.description: Lists the parts of the CURRENT multi (see select_multi) that play a program, with the program's name; parts are numbered from 1. It acts on the sampler's memory, not on disk: nothing is saved, and the change is lost if the sampler is switched off without saving the program from its front panel.
tools.name: get_part_programs
tools.title: Read what the parts of the current multi play

tools.description: Reads the sampler's own settings: its name, its clock and date, its play mode (multi, program, sample or muted) and whether its front panel is locked. It changes nothing.
tools.name: get_sampler_settings
tools.title: Read the sampler's name, clock, play mode and front-panel lock

tools.description: Sets one of the sampler's own settings and reads it back. 'name': 1 to 20 characters of plain ASCII. 'clock': YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS (the day of the week is worked out). 'play_mode': multi, program, sample, muted; muted plays nothing until another mode is set. 'front_panel': normal, locked; a locked front panel is unlocked only by setting it to normal. A value that is not valid is refused and nothing is sent.

value.description: The new value, in the form the description gives for that setting.

tools.name: set_sampler_setting
tools.title: Set the sampler's name, clock, play mode or front-panel lock

tools.description: Sets one switch of the sampler's MIDI setup (UTILITIES, MIDI SETUP). 'program_change': on, off (remote selection of programs within parts). 'multi_select': off, program_change, bank (how multis are selected remotely). 'multi_select_channel': a MIDI channel 1 to 16 with its port A or B (the port is A when left out), such as 3 or 3B (it has no effect while multi_select is off). 'external_apm_controller': a MIDI controller number, 0 to 127, the source in the APM matrix. 'aftertouch': channel, polyphonic. The sampler cannot be asked what these held before, so the answer cannot say, and this server cannot put the previous value back. A value that is not valid is refused and nothing is sent.

value.description: The new value, in the form the description gives for that switch.

tools.name: set_midi_setting
tools.title: Set one switch of the sampler's MIDI setup

tools.description: Sets the sampler's MIDI filter for one type of event (note_on, aftertouch, wheels, volume) on one MIDI channel: 'allow' lets the sampler respond to those messages, 'ignore' makes it ignore them. The channel is a MIDI channel 1 to 16 with its port A or B (the port is A when left out), such as 3 or 3B. The sampler cannot be asked what the filter was before, so the answer cannot say, and this server cannot put it back. A value that is not valid is refused and nothing is sent.

action.description: Whether the sampler allows or ignores those events.

channel.description: The MIDI channel: 1 to 16, or a text with its port such as "3B".

tools.name: set_midi_filter
tools.title: Allow or ignore a type of MIDI event on a channel

Connected to the sampler (DeviceID 0).
3 programs in memory.
Current program: BASS, 3 keygroups.

Selected the program "BASS" (3 keygroups).

Parameters (values are in the sampler's own units):

lfo 2: The program's second low-frequency oscillator.
- lfo 2 rate: 0 to 100. The speed of LFO 2. Per program. Also called: lfo2 speed.
- lfo 2 delay: 0 to 100. The time LFO 2's modulation takes to fade in. Per program.
- lfo 2 depth: 0 to 100. The initial depth of LFO 2's modulation. Per program.
- lfo 2 waveform: one of: SINE (0), TRIANGLE (1), SQUARE (2), SQUARE+ (3), SQUARE- (4), SAW BI (5), SAW UP (6), SAW DOWN (7), RANDOM (8). The waveform of LFO 2, one of nine. Per program. Also called: lfo2 shape.
- lfo 2 retrigger: on or off. Whether LFO 2 starts its cycle again on each new note (re-trigger, LFO 2 only). Per program.
- lfo 2 rate modulation source: one of: NO SOURCE (0), MODWHEEL (1), BEND (2), AFTERTOUCH (3), EXTERNAL (4), VELOCITY (5), KEYBOARD (6), LFO1 (7), LFO2 (8), AMP ENV (9), FILT ENV (10), AUX ENV (11), MODWHEEL 2 (12), BEND 2 (13), EXTERNAL 2 (14). The source that moves the rate of LFO 2. A source of the sampler's modulation matrix (spec Table 15). Codes 12 to 14 repeat MODWHEEL, BEND and EXTERNAL; what sets them apart from the first three is not documented. Per program.
- lfo 2 rate modulation amount: -100 to 100. How much the source moves the rate of LFO 2, as a signed amount. Per program.
- lfo 2 delay modulation source: one of: NO SOURCE (0), MODWHEEL (1), BEND (2), AFTERTOUCH (3), EXTERNAL (4), VELOCITY (5), KEYBOARD (6), LFO1 (7), LFO2 (8), AMP ENV (9), FILT ENV (10), AUX ENV (11), MODWHEEL 2 (12), BEND 2 (13), EXTERNAL 2 (14). The source that moves the delay of LFO 2. A source of the sampler's modulation matrix (spec Table 15). Codes 12 to 14 repeat MODWHEEL, BEND and EXTERNAL; what sets them apart from the first three is not documented. Per program.
- lfo 2 delay modulation amount: -100 to 100. How much the source moves the delay of LFO 2, as a signed amount. Per program.
- lfo 2 depth modulation source: one of: NO SOURCE (0), MODWHEEL (1), BEND (2), AFTERTOUCH (3), EXTERNAL (4), VELOCITY (5), KEYBOARD (6), LFO1 (7), LFO2 (8), AMP ENV (9), FILT ENV (10), AUX ENV (11), MODWHEEL 2 (12), BEND 2 (13), EXTERNAL 2 (14). The source that moves the depth of LFO 2. A source of the sampler's modulation matrix (spec Table 15). Codes 12 to 14 repeat MODWHEEL, BEND and EXTERNAL; what sets them apart from the first three is not documented. Per program.
- lfo 2 depth modulation amount: -100 to 100. How much the source moves the depth of LFO 2, as a signed amount. Per program.
- lfo 2 clock sync: on or off. Whether LFO 2 follows the MIDI clock (LFO 2 only). Per program. Also called: lfo 2 midi clock sync.
- lfo 2 clock division: one of: 8 cycles per beat (0), 6 cycles per beat (1), 4 cycles per beat (2), 3 cycles per beat (3), 2 cycles per beat (4), 1 cycle per beat (5), 2 beats per cycle (6), 3 beats per cycle (7), 4 beats per cycle (8), 5 beats per cycle (9), 6 beats per cycle (10), 7 beats per cycle (11), 8 beats per cycle (12), 9 beats per cycle (13), 10 beats per cycle (14), 11 beats per cycle (15), 12 beats per cycle (16), 13 beats per cycle (17), 14 beats per cycle (18), 15 beats per cycle (19), 16 beats per cycle (20), 17 beats per cycle (21), 18 beats per cycle (22), 19 beats per cycle (23), 20 beats per cycle (24), 21 beats per cycle (25), 22 beats per cycle (26), 23 beats per cycle (27), 24 beats per cycle (28), 25 beats per cycle (29), 26 beats per cycle (30), 27 beats per cycle (31), 28 beats per cycle (32), 29 beats per cycle (33), 30 beats per cycle (34), 31 beats per cycle (35), 32 beats per cycle (36), 33 beats per cycle (37), 34 beats per cycle (38), 35 beats per cycle (39), 36 beats per cycle (40), 37 beats per cycle (41), 38 beats per cycle (42), 39 beats per cycle (43), 40 beats per cycle (44), 41 beats per cycle (45), 42 beats per cycle (46), 43 beats per cycle (47), 44 beats per cycle (48), 45 beats per cycle (49), 46 beats per cycle (50), 47 beats per cycle (51), 48 beats per cycle (52), 49 beats per cycle (53), 50 beats per cycle (54), 51 beats per cycle (55), 52 beats per cycle (56), 53 beats per cycle (57), 54 beats per cycle (58), 55 beats per cycle (59), 56 beats per cycle (60), 57 beats per cycle (61), 58 beats per cycle (62), 59 beats per cycle (63), 60 beats per cycle (64), 61 beats per cycle (65), 62 beats per cycle (66), 63 beats per cycle (67), 64 beats per cycle (68). How LFO 2's cycle divides the MIDI clock when it follows it: from 8 cycles per beat to 64 beats per cycle (LFO 2 only). Per program. Also called: lfo 2 midi clock division.

result.instructions: This server edits a program of an AKAI S5000/S6000 sampler. Call get_status to see which program is current, list_programs and select_program to change it, and list_parameters to learn the parameter names and what each accepts: the filter, the amplitude envelope, the filter envelope and the two LFOs. Use get_parameters to read values and set_parameter to change one. Values are in the sampler's own units (0 to 100 for most), signed values are plain signed numbers, and choices are named as the sampler's screen names them (for example "2-POLE LP+"). create_program, rename_program and delete_program change the list of programs: delete_program deletes only the current program and only when its name is given as 'confirm'. list_samples, select_sample, get_sample_parameters and set_sample_parameter edit the samples in the same way (list_parameters with the domain "sample" names their parameters); no tool creates, deletes or loads a sample. list_multis, select_multi, get_multi_parameters and set_multi_parameter edit the parts of a multi (parts are numbered from 1; no tool creates, deletes or renames a multi). Changes act on the sampler's memory, not on disk; nothing is saved by this server.
